title: Review state registration
summary: Check whether you need to register in states where you have employees or offices, and file the foreign qualifications that apply. California draws the line at transacting intrastate business and the $800 minimum tax follows qualification (rule card us-ca.foreign-qualification); Texas adds late filing fees when registration comes more than 90 days after first transacting business (rule card us-tx.foreign-registration).

parts.title: List employee locations
parts.guidance: Reconcile where employees and contractors actually work with HR, payroll and managers. Capture state, start date, arrangement and expected moves without unnecessary personal details. Add offices, facilities and other business presence separately. Resolve uncertain locations before using the list for corporate-registration or tax analysis, and establish how future moves reach the team maintaining it.

parts.title: Check foreign qualification needs
parts.guidance: Review the location facts, entity form and activities in each state against its foreign-qualification rules and exemptions. Document the basis for filing, not filing or obtaining more facts. Resolve ambiguous cases with counsel before the company commits to a registration. Payroll, tax and licensing questions need separate treatment because their tests may differ.

parts.title: File foreign qualifications on the state portals
parts.guidance: Use the reviewed state-registration plan to assemble the application, home-state documents and local agent details. Check the destination’s current requirements, including signer authority and any certificate validity limit. Use the entity’s required signer and authorized filing process for submission and fees. Respond to corrections until accepted, then capture the issued entity number and ongoing state obligations.

verify.how: The entity appears in each state's business search with a foreign-qualification registration number.

metadata.supportReason: An agent can map employee locations to registration duties; the foreign-qualification filings themselves are state-portal form work.

geoNotes.summary: The federal texture is real: employees or premises in a new state typically mean a fresh GST registration for that state, plus state professional tax and a shops-and-establishments registration — India's version of foreign qualification.
Inside the UK there is nothing to qualify for; the concept appears at the border — a foreign company opening a UK establishment registers it at Companies House with form OS IN01 within a month.

The analog is municipal: each additional Betriebsstätte (office/branch) needs its own Gewerbeanmeldung with that municipality, and Gewerbesteuer is then apportioned across them — the ministry's founders portal covers the mechanics.
A new office is an établissement secondaire: declared through the guichet unique, which issues a per-establishment SIRET — a formality rather than a qualification battle.

No sub-national layer to qualify into: one commercial registry and one tax registration cover the whole country — the concept only appears at the border, where a foreign company opening a Portuguese branch registers a representação permanente.

The concept genuinely exists: carrying on business in a province means extra-provincial registration there — a federal corporation still registers in each province where it operates (some provinces have joint-registration agreements).
geoNotes.actionLabel: Register in a province or territory
